name: sanitize_document
description: Scrub an open session document: removes revision ids, authorship, embedded EXIF, hidden text PII, tracked revisions, comments, and (on request) macro/active parts through the same engine scrub path CLI sanitize calls. Body text is kept. Options mirror the engine scrub keys 1:1 (zeroRetention, purgeRSIDs, purgeAuthors, purgeExif, purgePII, acceptAllRevisions, stripComments, replacementAuthor, allowMacros, stripMacros); omitted options take engine defaults. allowMacros and stripMacros together fail with E_VALIDATION. Returns {ok:true,sessionId,revision,dirty,removedRSIDs,purgedAuthors,strippedExifBytes,purgedPII,bodyPII,acceptedRevisions,strippedComments,strippedMacros,macroParts,filesTouched,droppedRogue,...} plus the standard redoCleared signal when a redo chain is dropped. Example {"sessionId":"sess_abc","stripMacros":true} -> scrubbed session at a new revision (save after). IDs are session-scoped: valid only in the issuing session, must not be stored across sessions. ECMA-376 essentials: colors are hex without # (e.g. 4F46E5, never #4F46E5); font sizes are half-points in w:sz (e.g. 28 = 14pt, 22 = 11pt); spacing/margins/cellMar use twips dxa (twentieths of a point, e.g. 240 = 12pt, 180 = 9pt); borders use eighths-of-a-point sz (e.g. 32 = 4pt left accent). Workflow: open_document -> inspect_document -> search_content -> execute_batch -> save_document -> close_document. Always inspect first, batch second, save third. Single edit = 1-item batch. Never call twice when once suffices.
